task_row_model.query: For a 65-year-old patient with atrial fibrillation on warfarin scheduled for colonoscopy with planned polypectomy, how long before the procedure should warfarin be stopped, when should INR be checked, should the patient be bridged with LMWH, and when should anticoagulation be resumed?

documents.content: Clinical Endoscopy Guidelines (extract): For patients taking warfarin who are undergoing gastrointestinal procedures with possible mucosal biopsy or polypectomy, stop warfarin five days before the procedure to allow the INR to fall. Verify INR on the day of the procedure; many centers use a threshold of <1.5 before proceeding with interventions that carry bleeding risk. Routine immediate reversal is not recommended unless urgent hemostasis is required. Following uncomplicated polypectomy and satisfactory hemostasis, oral anticoagulation can usually be restarted at the prior dose approximately 24 hours after the procedure. (Note: a brief historical note on warfarin discovery appears in the full guideline and does not affect peri-procedural timing.)
documents.reasoning_trace: Gives core timing: stop warfarin 5 days pre-procedure, check INR day-of with <1.5 threshold, and resume warfarin ~24 hours after if hemostasis.

documents.content: Hospital Anticoagulation Bulletin (news style): Managing thromboembolic risk around endoscopy requires individualized assessment. Patients with very high thromboembolic risk—mechanical heart valves, recent thromboembolism, or recent stroke—are candidates for bridging anticoagulation. When bridging is used, therapeutic low-molecular-weight heparin (LMWH) is typically held 24 hours before an invasive procedure and restarted after bleeding risk is acceptable; many services resume LMWH 48–72 hours post-procedure depending on hemostasis. The bulletin contrasts DOAC and warfarin management and includes procedural complication rates and local audit statistics as background context, which are not prescriptive for timing.
documents.reasoning_trace: States criteria for bridging (high TE risk) and LMWH timing: stop 24 hours pre-procedure, resume 48–72 hours post-procedure if hemostasis.

documents.content: Endoscopy unit nursing memo (informal): For routine atrial fibrillation patients on warfarin coming for colonoscopy with possible polypectomy, the usual practice is to stop warfarin five days beforehand and recheck INR on arrival. If the polypectomy is uncomplicated and there is clear hemostasis, we often restart warfarin about 24 hours later; for cases with more extensive mucosal injury or stigmata of bleeding some clinicians delay restarting for 48 hours. For patients deemed high thrombotic risk the endoscopist coordinates with cardiology about bridging with LMWH — bridging increases complexity and requires holding LMWH 24 hours pre-procedure and resumption only after bleeding risk is acceptable.
documents.reasoning_trace: Reinforces stop-5-days and day-of INR check; restart warfarin ~24 hours if hemostasis, delayed to 48 hours if higher bleeding risk; notes bridging coordination and LMWH hold/resume timing.

task_row_model.golden_answer: Stop warfarin five days before the colonoscopy and verify the INR on the day of the procedure (commonly require INR <1.5). For routine AF without high thromboembolic risk, do not bridge. For high-risk patients (mechanical valve, recent stroke/VTE), consider therapeutic LMWH bridging: hold LMWH 24 hours before the procedure and resume LMWH 48–72 hours after once hemostasis is acceptable. Restart warfarin about 24 hours post-procedure if hemostasis; delay longer (≈48 hours) for higher bleeding risk.
